title: Finite Q3 split-operator equality on common rooted balls
question: For the actual finite-dimensional Q3 onsite-plus-all-bond split products on path4 and path6, does a local observable at site 1 agree while the tested rooted ball agrees, and does the first external edge produce a nonzero difference at the order-dependent first reachable split count?

model.split_step: U_delta=product of exact spectral exp(-i sign delta h_term/hbar) factors with the declared term order
model.observable: A=(exp(i (1/3) q_2) on the source site) and A*
model.embedding: path4 acts on sites 0..3 and is tensored with identities on sites 4,5 before comparison with path6
model.shape_test: Both paths have the same rooted induced radius-2 ball at source site 1; the first external edge is (3,4).

adversarial_review.check: d=2 is a bounded matrix fixture only; no CCR or unbounded-domain statement is inferred.
Both declared term orders, both time signs, and A/A* are evaluated with exact spectral factors.
Steps 0,1,2 are required below tolerance while step 3 is required above the declared witness floor.
The comparison is a full embedded operator norm, not only a support-set comparison.
Only path4/path6 with one source and radius two are tested; arbitrary graphs and all-shape uniformity remain open.
Finite matrix eigendecompositions are checked for finite values and the tolerance/floor are explicit manifest inputs.
No analytic Trotter rate, common core, D/delta-D Cauchy estimate, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure is claimed.
Lean R337 is reused for the rooted path-ball fixture; Python carries the finite matrix identity.

lean_crosscheck.role: R337 checks the exact rooted path-ball fixture and scalar BCH bookkeeping; Python checks the full finite matrix split products.

qft_interface.closed: At fixed split counts before the order-dependent first external step, the two finite products agree on the embedded local observable; the first reachable external edge (3,4) has an explicit nonzero witness at N=3 for onsite-then-bonds and N=4 for reverse order.
qft_interface.open: A volume- and cutoff-uniform analytic Trotter rate, unbounded common core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy estimate, exhaustion interchange, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: This is a claim-nonbearing finite Q3 interface only; it supplies no heat-root-incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure.

next_action: Use the finite operator equality as a local input while attempting a uniform graph-Lipschitz/Trotter estimate on a declared common core; if the estimate depends on volume, cutoff, shape or split count, record that obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite matrix shape test. It is not an exhaustion-independent thermodynamic dynamics theorem and does not close any Clay or QFT gate.
no_overclaim: The result is limited to the declared d=3 path4/path6 matrices and fixed split counts. It does not establish an N-to-infinity limit, arbitrary-shape independence, a common generator, KMS/GNS reconstruction, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
